answer: An ivory-tower identity score proves nothing until each agent’s claimed origin is geolocated against independent imagery, so registration requires a live capture whose shadows, signage, and terrain match a known site. A lantern-lit storefront photo fails when sun-angle and street-furniture checks contradict the claimed latitude, forcing attackers to stage physical scenes per identity. That signal costs forgery of consistent geometry across many sites, yet reuse of one verified location still slips through, capping the mechanism at costly, not impossible.
